text: Russia's plan for Kyiv in February 2022 was a coup de main in which intelligence operatives inside Kyiv would seize government buildings.
Under Russia's February 2022 plan the VDV would take Antonov airport at Hostomel to establish an airbridge.
Under Russia's February 2022 plan mechanised forces would advance on Kyiv on both banks of the Dnipro, with a new regime installed within two or three days.

text: On 24 Feb 2022 about 34 helicopters landed 200–300 VDV troops at Hostomel.
Fewer than 200 National Guard conscripts held the VDV landing force at Hostomel for more than an hour on 24 Feb 2022 before withdrawing.

observations.note: time the defenders held before withdrawing

text: The follow-on Russian Il-76 airlift to Hostomel on 24 Feb 2022 was aborted in mid-air.
A Ukrainian counterattack at sunset on 24 Feb 2022 retook Hostomel airfield by 21:00 and cratered the runway.
The Russians had Hostomel airport back on 25 Feb 2022, but only when the mechanised column from Belarus arrived.
Behind Hostomel airport the Russian column stretched more than 40 miles (64 km) back towards Prybirsk and stalled.
Fuel, food, spare parts, mud, broken-down vehicles and Ukrainian ambushes are all blamed for the stalling of the Russian convoy north of Kyiv.
Ukrainian engineers blew most bridges on the western outskirts of Kyiv by 27 Feb 2022.
On 25 or 26 Feb 2022 a dam breach at Kozarovychi flooded the Irpin floodplain.

text: After the bridge demolitions and the flooding, Russia was left to attack through Bucha, Irpin and above all Moshchun.
At Moshchun an understrength battalion of the 72nd Mechanised Brigade held the Irpin river line.
East of the Dnipro the Russian columns advancing on Kyiv were stopped at Chernihiv and at Brovary in 2022.
ISW judged on 19 Mar 2022 that the Russian campaign to seize Kyiv had failed.
On 29 Mar 2022 Russia announced in Istanbul that it would "drastically reduce" activity around Kyiv and Chernihiv.
On 2 Apr 2022 Deputy Defence Minister Maliar declared the whole Kyiv region liberated.
The Russian withdrawal from the Kyiv region in 2022 revealed the killings in Bucha.
Russian forces never entered Kyiv in 2022 and took no ground inside the city limits.
The Ukrainian Irpin line held from Stoianka to Demydiv in 2022.
The Russians reached Bucha, Hostomel, Vorzel, part of Irpin and the north-western half of Moshchun, but never crossed in force east of the Irpin River south of Moshchun.
Hostomel airport fell to the Russians at about 13:00 on 24 Feb 2022, was retaken by Ukraine by 21:00 and was lost for good on 25 Feb.
Hostomel airport was denied to Russia as an airbridge: no Il-76 landed there on 25 Feb 2022 and the runway was cratered.

The c01 weather data are ERA5 reanalysis at Antonov airport: a model, not observations, in local time; Ukraine moved to summer time on 27 Mar 2022.
ERA5 gives 24 Feb 2022 at Antonov airport as 1–5 °C, overcast (93%), 1.2 mm of light rain and wind of 10 km/h or less, with sunrise at 06:54 and sunset at 17:31.
BAR gives 24 Feb 2022 at Hostomel as 2–4 °C with light rain, sunrise 06:52 and sunset 17:30, matching ERA5.
The Ukrainian counterattack at Hostomel on 24 Feb 2022 opened at dusk.
ERA5 gives 25 Feb 2022 at Antonov airport as −0.4 to 7 °C, dry and clearing mid-morning, with sunset at 17:33; it was the link-up day.
ERA5 gives 26 Feb – 8 Mar 2022 at Antonov airport as −5 to 7 °C and mostly overcast, with sleet and wet snow on 1–2 Mar (4.1 mm) and snow on 8 Mar; sunset moved from 17:35 to 17:52.
From 26 Feb to 8 Mar 2022 the topsoil (0–7 cm) at Antonov airport stayed above 0 °C and wet (about 0.33–0.36 m³/m³) in ERA5: the ground was unfrozen, which fits the mud reports.
ERA5 gives 9–12 Mar 2022 at Antonov airport as a hard frost (−8 °C minimum), clear on 10–11 Mar, with sunset about 17:55; the topsoil froze briefly.
The Brovary ambush and the Moshchun assault fell in the hard-frost spell of 9–12 Mar 2022.
ERA5 gives 14–23 Mar 2022 at Antonov airport as dry and mostly clear with frosty nights, up to 16 °C on 23 Mar, and sunset about 18:05 to 18:16: good imagery days, such as Maxar's of 19 Mar.

ERA5 gives 29 Mar – 2 Apr 2022 at Antonov airport as rainy (8.1 mm on 1 Apr, 8.4 mm on 2 Apr) and overcast, with snow on 3 Apr; on 28 Mar sunrise was 06:44 and sunset 19:25. This was the period of the withdrawal and the Bucha discoveries.
Snow depth at Antonov airport stayed at 0–3 cm through 24 Feb – 6 Apr 2022 in ERA5.
MWI estimates about 50,000 Russian troops were committed against Kyiv in all.
The Russian Northern Front had about 30,000 troops from the 29th, 35th and 36th Combined Arms Armies of the Eastern Military District, staged in Belarus on the west bank of the Dnipro.
The Russian Northeastern Front had about 20,000 troops from the 41st and 2nd Combined Arms Armies of the Central Military District, on the east bank of the Dnipro.
Pavliuk claims about 70,000 Russian men and 7,000 armoured vehicles came from Belarus alone.
RUSI gives a 12:1 force ratio in Russia's favour on the Gomel axis.

observations.note: Russia : Ukraine on the Gomel axis

text: Russia formed group "V" at Gomel for the right bank and group "O" at Bryansk to encircle Kyiv from the left bank, both under the Eastern Military District command post.
Russian units moved in administrative column, were told to bypass resistance and expected to switch to stabilisation by D+10.

observations.subject: planned time to switch to stabilisation

text: Col. Gen. Aleksandr Chaiko, commander of the Eastern Military District, commanded the Russian forces against Kyiv.
The 31st Guards Air Assault Brigade and the 45th Guards Spetsnaz Brigade flew to Hostomel from Bolshoy Bokov, about 170 km north.
The 31st Guards Air Assault Brigade likely committed about 2,000 men in 2 BTGs around Kyiv.
Mediazona counted 34 dead of the 31st Guards Air Assault Brigade from 25 Feb to 7 Mar 2022.
HUR says up to 50 men of the 31st Guards Air Assault Brigade were killed at Hostomel.
The airlift on standby for Hostomel was the 76th Guards Air Assault Division at Pskov, with 18 Il-76s.
The 76th Division's 234th Regiment, the 56th Air Assault Regiment and the 64th Separate Motor Rifle Brigade were at Bucha.
The 64th (Khabarovsk) Motor Rifle Brigade deployed about 1,500 men and has at least 44 named dead for February–March 2022.
The 331st Guards Parachute Regiment lost its commander and at least 39 others.

observations.value_text: its commander and at least 39 others
observations.subject: 331st Regiment dead

text: Ukraine's General Staff said the 106th VDV Division had 2 BTGs withdrawn on 27 Mar 2022.

claimants.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

text: The Russian 37th Motor Rifle Brigade and 5th Tank Brigade (36th Combined Arms Army) pushed on Makariv and Yasnohorodka.
The Russian 155th and 40th Naval Infantry Brigades came in as replacements around Kyiv by 19 Mar 2022.
Some Russian naval infantry units around Kyiv reportedly lost up to 90%.
Rosgvardia OMON/SOBR from Kemerovo and Chechen units fought on the west bank; the Chechens were geolocated at Borodianka.
The Russian 165th Artillery Brigade (35th Combined Arms Army) fought on the Kyiv axis.
On the east bank the 90th Guards Tank Division (6th and 239th Tank Regiments), with the 2nd and 41st Combined Arms Armies, advanced against Brovary and Chernihiv.
The 41st Combined Arms Army had about 30,000 troops at Chernihiv.
The Russian convoy north of Kyiv carried an estimated 15,000 troops.
The Russian convoy included fuel tankers, food and ammunition trucks, towed and self-propelled artillery, BMP-3s and tanks.
Pavliuk mentions about 2,000 guards for the Russian convoy.
From 27 Feb to 2 Mar 2022 the Russian forces near Kyiv paused for 72 hours, then formed ad hoc groupings of battalions.
From 9 Mar 2022 Russia committed 2–5 BTGs at a time around Kyiv.
Russian forces near Kyiv were digging in from 19 Mar 2022.
Damaged Russian units were rotated to Belarus from 27 Mar 2022.
From 1 Apr 2022 Russia withdrew from the Kyiv area behind a screen of the 38th and 37th Motor Rifle Brigades and the 5th Tank Brigade.
By 4–6 Apr 2022 ISW assessed the Russian Kyiv force as "likely a spent force".
MWI says Ukraine's formal units defending Kyiv numbered 3,000–5,000, and the whole force up to 18,000, mostly Territorial Defence and volunteers.
Wikipedia's infobox gives the Ukrainian northern-front force as 20,000 soldiers and 18,000 irregulars.
Before the invasion more than 10 Ukrainian brigades, about half the manoeuvre force, were in Donbas, while Kyiv held one manoeuvre brigade and two artillery brigades.

observations.subject: share of the manoeuvre force in Donbas

text: Col. Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi commanded the defence of Kyiv.
The Kyiv Defence Council (Syrskyi, Mayor Klitschko, Lt. Gen. Pavliuk) formed on 24 Feb 2022.
Syrskyi set up two defensive rings around Kyiv, the suburbs and the city, with sectors under generals from the military schools.
From 15 Mar 2022 Pavliuk headed the Kyiv Regional Military Administration.
The 72nd Mechanised Brigade, under Col. Oleksandr Vdovychenko, came from Bila Tserkva about 85 km south of Kyiv.
The 1st and 3rd Battalions of the 72nd Mechanised Brigade were on the east side of the Dnipro, covering about 30 km.
The 2nd Battalion of the 72nd Mechanised Brigade was on the Irpin, covering about 22 km, and some of its companies had only 22 men.
In the 2nd Battalion of the 72nd Brigade, the 4th Company held Bucha–Irpin and the E373, the 5th Company Moshchun–Chervone (fewer than 30 men at first), and the 6th Company Huta-Mezhyhirska–Liutizh.
The 72nd Mechanised Brigade's artillery group had 2S1, 2S3, BM-21 and MT-12 battalions.
The National Guard's 4th Rapid Reaction Brigade, under Maj. Vitalii Rudenko, held Hostomel.
The 4th Rapid Reaction Brigade's rear echelon left at Hostomel numbered about 200 (WOTR), fewer than 200 (BAR) or about 300 (WaPo).
The Hostomel defenders had small arms, a few BTRs, Igla MANPADS, a ZU-23-2 and two D-30s in Horenka.
The 80th and 95th Air Assault Brigades fought in the 24 Feb counterattack, at Makariv, and as reinforcements at Moshchun.
The 14th Mechanised Brigade fought at Makariv.
The 70th Support Brigade carried out bridge demolitions around Kyiv.
Ukrainian training-centre artillery, including 2S7 Pions, moved out of its bases to defend Kyiv.
The SSO's 3rd Special Purpose Regiment fought in the defence of Kyiv.
Pavliuk credits a 30-man SSO unit with disabling the Russian convoy's lead three vehicles.
HUR teams fought around Kyiv, with the Georgian Legion mostly under HUR at the airport.
The police KORD unit fought at Huta-Mezhyhirska.
By Lt. Col. Yaroslav Honchar's account, Aerorozvidka had about 30 special-forces troops and drone operators on quad bikes.
Aerorozvidka had 50 R18 octocopter sets by 24 Feb 2022.
The Kyiv city 112th Territorial Defence Brigade had nine battalions, was full within three days and manned hundreds of roadblocks.

observations.subject: 112th TDF Brigade filled
observations.note: unit day; the metric's default unit is month

text: Almost 100,000 Ukrainians had volunteered for the Territorial Defence Forces by 6 Mar 2022.
MWI says 25,000 rifles and 10 million rounds were handed out in Kyiv.
The International Legion was created on 27 Feb 2022; Kuleba claimed 20,000+ volunteers, against 1,500–2,000 actual foreign fighters per 2023 investigations.
The 40th Tactical Aviation Brigade's MiG-29s flew from Vasylkiv and were dispersed before the first Russian strike.
Ukraine had about 50 MiG-29s and 32 Su-27s in all in February 2022.
Ukrainian Su-24s and Su-25s flew strikes in the defence of Kyiv.
"Fewer than a dozen" Ukrainian TB2s were operational during the Battle of Kyiv.
At Chernihiv the defenders were the 1st Tank Brigade (Col. Leonid Khoda, about 2,000), the 58th Motorised Brigade and the 27th National Guard Regiment, about 6,000 in all.
RUSI gives Russia 2,433 barrel artillery systems against Ukraine's 1,176.
Ukraine kept artillery parity for about the first 1.5 months and "blunted Russia's attempt to seize Kyiv using massed fires from two artillery brigades".

cites.quote: blunted Russia's attempt to seize Kyiv using massed fires from two artillery brigades

text: For a few days the Kyiv forces risked running out of 152 mm ammunition.
Massed fires from two Ukrainian artillery brigades blunted the Russian drive on Kyiv.
The 72nd Mechanised Brigade's 2S3 batteries rotated between four positions each.
Ukrainian artillery fired on the runway at Hostomel.
Ukrainian artillery fired on Russian pontoon sites plotted in advance.
Ukrainian artillery fire was called in over WhatsApp.
Ukrainian artillery fire was also called in from civilian phone calls: an artillery strike destroyed a Russian refuelling point after a woman phoned it in.
Ukraine blew bridges around Kyiv on 25–27 Feb 2022, though few on day one.
Two dam and sluice breaches flooded the Irpin floodplain.
Russian intelligence "did not foresee the use of hydrotechnical structures".

cites.quote: did not foresee the use of hydrotechnical structures

text: The Russians made "a dozen or more wet gap crossings" of the Irpin with pontoons, and most were destroyed by fire.

cites.quote: a dozen or more wet gap crossings

text: RFE/RL says there were three Russian pontoons at Moshchun, two of them destroyed.
At Vokzalna Street Ukrainians hit the lead Russian vehicle with an ATGM and the trail vehicle with an RPG, then fired artillery for 10–20 minutes on a column in "parade formation".

observations.subject: artillery fire on the trapped column

text: At Irpin Ukrainians used NLAWs on the lead and trail Russian vehicles.
The Brovary ambush (vignette v01) was a head-and-tail ambush.
According to a US official, Javelins at the Russian convoy's head made "a roadblock".
Aerorozvidka's night teams carried thermal drones, 1.5 kg bomblets, night-vision goggles, sniper rifles and remote mines.
Aerorozvidka teams launched drones when Russian jamming was off and ran after launch.
Aerorozvidka teams prioritised Russian EW vehicles and fed Delta and Starlink data to the artillery.
A Furia UAV cued Ukrainian fire on the Rakivka pontoon.
Russian jamming at Moshchun "made Ukrainian drones inoperable".
Ukrainian TB2s hit Russian SAMs, guns and trucks early on, but their emissions made them trackable.
At the start of the invasion jamming and decoys hit Ukraine's S-300 and Buk hardest "to the north of Kyiv along the Hostomel/Irpin and Chernihiv axes".

cites.quote: to the north of Kyiv along the Hostomel/Irpin and Chernihiv axes

text: Ukrainian fighters carried the air defence of Kyiv for the first days of the invasion.
Two Ukrainian SAM sites screening the Dnipro were destroyed at the start of the invasion, which opened the helicopter route to Hostomel.
Russian SAMs assumed "anything flying was Russian".
From 3 Mar 2022 lone Ukrainian Buk TELARs and surviving S-300s acted as "pop-up" threats and made medium altitude "prohibitively dangerous" for Russian aircraft.
The VKS flew at 500 ft or below and lost at least eight jets in a week.

observations.subject: Russian jets lost in a week

notes: week dated from the section 10 phasing

text: Stinger and Igla MANPADS were "a major factor" in Russian air losses.
Russian Su-35S combat air patrols with R-77-1s outranged Ukraine's R-27s, at odds of "up to 15:2" (6:2 per Zabrodskyi).

observations.note: Russia : Ukraine odds in air engagements (Bronk)

text: S-400s and a Podlet-K1 radar in Belarus forced Ukrainian jets below 100 ft.
From 9 Mar 2022 the VKS switched to night Su-34 sorties, because Ukrainian MANPADS crews lacked night-vision goggles.
Ukraine deconflicted its jets and SAMs by time slots until 3 Mar 2022, then by areas after friendly fire.
Russian Ka-52s led the gunships and suffered disproportionately; they often failed to dispense flares when engaged by MANPADS.
Russian columns carried 3–4 days of supply and used Belarusian railways.
Russian forces north of Kyiv were short of fuel, food and spare parts.
The BBC adds tyres, the mud and C2 failures to the Russian convoy's problems.
By 22 Mar 2022 some Russian troops had frostbite for lack of winter gear.
Russia covered its withdrawal from Kyiv with heavy artillery, mined the routes and blew bridges Ukraine had failed to destroy on day one.

measure: pontoon and river crossings of the Irpin
effect: widened the river from 10–20 m to a lake over 400 m wide in places
rationale: The breaches of the Kozarovychi dam flooded the Irpin floodplain, which had been easy to pontoon.

counter: pre-plotted artillery fire on pontoon sites
measure: Russian wet gap crossings with pontoons
effect: most pontoon crossings destroyed by fire
rationale: Ukrainian artillery fired on pontoon sites plotted in advance, and most of the dozen or more Russian crossings were destroyed by fire.

effect: denied crossings and forced attacks through Bucha, Irpin and Moshchun
rationale: Blowing most bridges on the western outskirts by 27 Feb left Russia to attack through Bucha, Irpin and Moshchun.
At Vokzalna Street an ATGM hit the lead vehicle and an RPG the trail vehicle, then artillery fired on the trapped column.

effect: at least eight jets lost in a week
rationale: The VKS flew at 500 ft or below and lost at least eight jets in a week; Stinger and Igla were a major factor.

effect: MANPADS crews without night-vision goggles could not engage
rationale: From 9 Mar the VKS switched to night Su-34 sorties because MANPADS crews lacked night-vision goggles.
From 3 Mar lone Buk TELARs and surviving S-300s acted as pop-up threats.

counter: S-400 and Podlet-K1 radar umbrella from Belarus
rationale: S-400s and a Podlet-K1 radar in Belarus forced Ukrainian jets below 100 ft.
Su-35S CAPs with R-77-1s outranged Ukraine's R-27s at up to 15:2 odds.

effect: made Ukrainian drones inoperable at Moshchun
rationale: Russian jamming at Moshchun made Ukrainian drones inoperable.

effect: drones flown in gaps of the jamming
rationale: Aerorozvidka teams launched when Russian jamming was off and ran after launch.

effect: degraded Ukrainian SAMs north of Kyiv in the opening days
rationale: Jamming and decoys hit S-300 and Buk hardest north of Kyiv at the start.

effect: Ka-52s suffered disproportionately, often failing to dispense flares
rationale: Ka-52s led the gunships and suffered disproportionately; they often failed to dispense flares when engaged by MANPADS.

text: About 34 Russian helicopters ran low up the Dnipro past the Kyiv dam on 24 Feb 2022, where a Ka-52 and a Mi-24 went down; then MiG-29s dived in, and the stream reached Hostomel through low cloud.
A 25-year-old National Guard Igla gunner let a strafing Ka-52 pass inside minimum range, re-acquired it and dropped it onto the Hostomel runway as an extra obstacle.

In the sunset counterattack of 24 Feb 2022 artillery and Su-24 bombs fell on Hostomel airfield at dusk; the 4th Rapid Reaction Brigade raised a shrapnel-torn flag by 21:00, then the Ukrainians cratered the runway and pulled out.
The An-225 Mriya burned in its hangar while the Russians held Hostomel airport.
The An-225 Mriya was ready to fly by 22:00 on 23 Feb 2022, but no order came to evacuate it.
notes: 'to evacuate it' is implied by 'ready to fly ... no order came'

text: The 64 km Russian column of tankers, trucks and guns stood two or three abreast on the P02, stalled for days.
At night Aerorozvidka quad bikes slipped out of the forest near Ivankiv, and drones bombed the convoy's lead vehicles and then the depot.
notes: undated; order per the Guardian original (lead vehicles first, then the depot)

text: On Vokzalna Street the Bucha column was trapped "in what would best be described as a parade formation" between two hits and destroyed by artillery.

cites.quote: in what would best be described as a parade formation

text: A Bucha pensioner fired a captured grenade launcher at a Russian fuel truck.
notes: dated to the Vokzalna Street set piece of 27 Feb

text: Two civilian 4×4s carried nearly a ton of explosives to the Kozarovychi dam, which went at 13:30, and the river widened into a lake.

observations.subject: explosives carried
observations.note: mass of explosives, not TNT equivalent; unit t

text: Civilians fleeing Irpin climbed over the rubble of the P30 bridge at Romanivka and ran about 100 yards in the open under mortar fire.
At Moshchun Russian pontoons went in at Rakivka; every Ukrainian tube in range fired on 6 Mar 2022.
On 11 Mar 2022 the Russian assault at Moshchun came to within 10 m of the Ukrainian trenches; two tanks arrived, and a Russian voice came over the radio: "We cannot storm".

observations.subject: closest Russian approach to Ukrainian trenches

text: The Brovary ambush is the v01 vignette set piece.
The Ghost of Kyiv air-war set piece involves low-level MiG-29 sorties under Russian CAPs, a Su-27 lost over Kyiv on 25 Feb 2022, and MANPADS teams hunting low jets.
The Ghost of Kyiv was a myth.
As the Russian convoys rolled north into Belarus, bodies lay on Yablunska Street in Bucha that satellites had photographed on 19 Mar 2022.
Before the invasion Ukraine treated Kyiv as an economy-of-force sector and the northern Russian group as a diversion.

mentions.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

text: Ukraine's redeployment north came about 7 hours before the invasion of 24 Feb 2022.

observations.subject: redeployment order before the invasion
observations.note: unit h; metric default is min

text: Within the 72nd Mechanised Brigade two battalions went east of the Dnipro because the main Russian thrust was expected via Chernihiv, and the 2nd Battalion stayed at Bila Tserkva so as not to alarm locals.
Ukraine decided to disperse before the first Russian strike: command posts went to the field a week out, and aircraft and SAMs were dispersed hours before.
notes: 'a week out' read as about 17 Feb

text: The Russian opening strikes of 24 Feb 2022 found about 10% of Ukraine's mobile SAM sites.

observations.subject: mobile SAM sites found by the Russian opening strikes

text: RUSI calls Russia's air assault on a position (Hostomel), rather than along an axis, "extremely dangerous".
The Russian air assault on Hostomel had no armour or artillery, and the troops thought they were going to Grodno.
Russia's reason for aborting the Hostomel airlift on 24 Feb 2022 is debated: the slow seizure, the cratered runway, or fear for the transports after the helicopter losses.
Zaluzhnyi decided to counterattack Hostomel at once on 24 Feb 2022, over Vdovychenko's objection that he lacked the forces.
The Ukrainians chose to retake Hostomel airfield, crater it and withdraw rather than hold it against the Russian column.
Zelensky decided to stay in Kyiv; his guards and Arestovych urged him to leave, and he argued that flight would collapse the government.
Within days of the invasion Ukrainian officials decided to hand out rifles to civilians in Kyiv; military leaders bristled and later blamed it for friendly fire.
Panics over "saboteurs" followed the arming of civilians in Kyiv, in Obolon on 25 Feb and near the zoo on 26 Feb 2022.
Few bridges were blown on day one, which let the Russians reach the Irpin quickly.
The E373 bridge was half-dropped and mined, and the Moshchun bridge was overlooked on 27 Feb 2022.
Syrskyi decided to flood the Irpin (25/26 Feb 2022) and then to enlarge the breach (7–8 Mar); a civilian proposed it and Syrskyi "immediately endorsed it".
The risk of breaching the Kozarovychi dam was sweeping away villages downstream, and the first attempt failed.
The flooding funnelled the Russians into Hostomel, Bucha and Irpin.
To hit the Russian convoy Ukraine weighed air and TB2 strikes against the column's air defences, and chose small night teams at its head and depots.
Around 14 Mar 2022 (21 Mar per SWJ) Zaluzhnyi refused Vdovychenko's request to withdraw from Moshchun.
The fix at Moshchun was rotation every three days or less, a new battalion, and fire on the crossings.
The Ukrainians hesitated to shift forces west after Brovary, and moved only once the east went quiet, counterattacking at Moshchun on 19 Mar 2022.
Chaiko first tried to sever the roads west of Kyiv, took heavy losses under fire from both flanks, and withdrew when the left-bank effort failed.
Ukraine's General Staff claimed that reinforcement of the Kyiv grouping by the 5th Combined Arms Army was "refused" because of losses in the south.

claimants.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

text: Russia reframed and left Kyiv: Rudskoi's "first stage" claim came on 25 Mar 2022, then the Istanbul pledge on 29 Mar.
Ukraine's General Staff at first read the Russian pullback from Kyiv as "probably a rotation".

claimants.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

mentions.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

text: Ukrainian gunners first took the Russian covering barrage for a new offensive; by the time they realised it covered a withdrawal, the bridges were down.
Putin said in 2024 that there was "no political decision to storm" Kyiv.
notes: 'Was Kyiv a feint?' is debated; the claim is about 2022

text: MWI says the Russian plan for Kyiv had a single phase, the rapid seizure of the city.
ISW judged on 1 Apr 2022 that Kremlin claims that the north-east attacks were only meant to degrade Ukrainian forces are "false".
The Russian MoD claimed the capture of Hostomel involved some 200 helicopters and killed about 200 Ukrainians, with no Russian losses; the claim was met with scepticism.
A Ka-52 pilot told Russian TV: "In the first attack, we immediately lost the leader of our group".

cites.quote: In the first attack, we immediately lost the leader of our group

text: A captured Russian paratrooper said of the Ukrainian barrage of 26 Feb 2022 at Hostomel: "Almost nobody survived that day".
A captured 1st Guards Tank Army synchronisation matrix expected the "blocking and destruction of individual scattered units" by D+10.

cites.quote: blocking and destruction of individual scattered units

text: Russian planners assumed Ukraine could generate only about 40,000 more troops.

observations.subject: additional Ukrainian troops Russian planners assumed

text: Kremlin-run media claimed Russian paratroopers crossed the Irpin on 16 Mar 2022; ISW judged it likely false.
On 25 Mar 2022 Rudskoi said "the main tasks of the first stage of the operation" were complete and the "main goal" was Donbas.

cites.quote: the main tasks of the first stage of the operation

text: On 29 Mar 2022 Medinsky announced two "de-escalatory steps", including drastically reducing activity towards Kyiv and Chernihiv.
Russia presented its drawdown around Kyiv as a goodwill gesture.
Lavrov called the Bucha killings "staged"; the Russian MoD claimed the bodies were "moving" and that the mass grave held victims of Ukrainian strikes.
Satellite imagery from 19 Mar 2022 contradicts Russian claims that the Bucha killings were staged.
Putin honoured the 64th Motor Rifle Brigade on 18 Apr 2022.
The Kostroma VK memorial pages for the 331st Regiment said: "The 331st regiment is disappearing".
Leaked hospital data show 898 Russian servicemen treated in Gomel and Khoiniki after the march on Kyiv (an RFE/RL investigation, relayed).

observations.subject: servicemen treated in Gomel and Khoiniki hospitals

text: Putin said in June 2024: "There was no political decision to storm the three-million-strong city".

cites.quote: There was no political decision to storm the three-million-strong city
